target: Combined airborne fallout of the 946 CE Millennium eruption

sites.name: Lake Sihailongwan
sites.horizon: T2, colourless peak at 53 cm and light-brown peak at 52 cm
sites.inspection: Contiguous 2 cm range finders, followed by contiguous 1 cm point samples at detected peaks. Varve microfacies and glass chemistry examined.
sites.preservation: Annual laminae and unabraded shards. Sub-30 μm particles were excluded by the extraction. Sediment capture and mixing have not been calibrated to primary fallout.
sites.control: A black scoria layer (T1) was visible at 78–79 cm core depth. Its different age, composition and colour preclude a universal visual threshold.

sites.name: Quanyang peat
sites.inspection: Contiguous 1 cm slices. The authors found 20–25 pumice particles/cm³ at 64 cm and did not find large pumice in the adjacent 63 and 65 cm slices.
sites.preservation: Organic roots, dispersed pumice and uncertain fine fraction. The authors link the glass to Millennium pyroclastic material and consider ash lofted from pyroclastic flows.
sites.control: Pumice up to 3 mm across was identifiable in the peat. The source supplies no site calibration for detecting a bed of total fallout.
sites.reference: Han et al. 2019, section 1.1 and Fig. 1 (ledger key Sun19Q)

sites.name: Lake Kushu
sites.inspection: Invisible B-Tm tephra. The reported glass-shard concentration peaked at 30,671 per g dry sediment.
sites.preservation: Preserved microscopic glass. Primary loading, fine fraction and deposit bulk density are unavailable.
sites.control: Eastern archive comparison held out of all western sensitivity refits.
sites.reference: Chen et al. 2016, section 3.2 and Fig. 4, and Chen et al. 2019, RK12-0151

sites.name: Gushantun peat
sites.inspection: Reported age 260–420 cal yr BP. A compilation assigned the horizon to B-Tm.
sites.preservation: The disagreement concerns which eruption is represented.
sites.control: No independent designation of the Millennium horizon at this locality.
sites.reference: Zhao et al. 2012 and Costa et al. Table S1 P68

sites.name: Ulleung Basin 13PT-P4_026
sites.inspection: Identified as cryptotephra with 9,529 shards/g dry sediment. The two visible layers in the same Holocene sequence belong to other eruptions.
sites.preservation: Bioturbation, focusing, redistribution and the original bed-recognition response remain uncalibrated.
sites.control: Independent marine probe, withheld from all western likelihoods.
sites.reference: Chen22 | Costa24 P74, Chen22 Table 1 and sec. 2.1. Costa24 Table S1 P74, footnote.

sites.control: Independent marine probe, withheld from all western likelihoods.
sites.reference: Yang21 S1 row 50 | Ikehara et al., 2017 | Ikehara17, Tables 1 and 3

scenarios.title: One-slice effective visibility
scenarios.assumption: At these core horizons, 1 cm of original local fallout suffices for recognition as a continuous layer. One slice is the sampling scale. Its status as a visibility scale is an assumption.

scenarios.title: Ten-slice effective visibility
scenarios.assumption: A primary layer ten times the sampling interval suffices for a visible bed. This allows tenfold weaker net preservation or recognition than the one-slice scenario.

scenarios.title: Hold Quanyang out
scenarios.assumption: Condition on the lake alone at the one-slice scale. Predict the peat independently.

scenarios.title: Hold Sihailongwan out
scenarios.assumption: Condition on the peat alone at the one-slice scale. Predict the lake independently.

scenarios.title: Sub-slice visibility at the varved lake
scenarios.assumption: Effective original-fallout visibility scales of 1 mm at the varved lake and 1 cm in peat. Fine sampling and different lithology make this a sensitivity test only.

scenarios.title: Comparable visible fallout beds
scenarios.assumption: The original-fallout equivalent needed for a visible bed at the checked lake and peat is at most the thickness of a documented visible B-Tm bed in a comparable sedimentary setting. The Lake Ogawara OG12-2 visible layer is 1 cm. The margin of Larchenkov bog has a B-Tm ash layer up to 2 cm thick, while the central bog preserved cryptotephra. Matrix, sorting and preservation differ between archives. The model conditions on this transfer.

controls.measurement: B-Tm ash up to 2 cm at the margin. The centre has only cryptotephra.
controls.source: Razjigaeva et al. (2020), distribution of the ash layer
